children: U.S.-based employers announced 52,881 job cuts in August, up 58% from July, according to a report from global outplacement and executive coaching firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas.
Still, layoff plans are down 38% from the same month last year.
"This is the quietest August since 2022, but is generally on average for the month since the mid-2010s," said Andy Challenger, chief revenue officer for the firm.

Consumer products led all sectors in August with 10,057 cuts, driven by announcements at Procter & Gamble and Estée Lauder, the report said. Meanwhile, technology announced 6,103 cuts in August, its lowest monthly total of 2026.
Restructuring led all reasons for job cuts in August, outpacing artificial intelligence, which had five straight months leading the reason for cuts.
Meanwhile, employers announced plans to hire fell 23% in August from July.
"While companies are making plans to hire more workers than last year, according to our numbers, it doesn't appear those positions are being filled quickly," Challenger added.
The report precedes the August jobs report, which will be released Friday by the Labor Department. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal expect 53,000 jobs were added.

title: U.S. Employer Layoff Plans Rise, Hiring Plans Pullback
